subject.title: [Feature]: Surface embedded-runner startup phases to diagnostics consumers

question: Should OpenClaw add `run.execution_phase` as a stable diagnostic-bus contract for embedded-runner startup, or extend/reuse the existing generic phase event instead?
rationale: Both shapes are technically possible, but choosing a new closed event vocabulary versus broadening the generic phase contract establishes a lasting plugin and diagnostics API boundary.

options.title: Add the narrow run event
options.body: Accept the linked PR’s dedicated session-correlated event after confirming its naming, ordering, privacy, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Extend generic phase events
options.body: Require the implementation to enrich `diagnostic.phase.completed` with run/session semantics and prove that its duration-oriented consumers remain coherent.

options.title: Keep phases private
options.body: Decline a new diagnostic contract and direct external status consumers to coarser run/model/plugin-hook signals, accepting the startup visibility gap.

recommendation.title: Add the narrow run event
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR’s dedicated session-correlated event after confirming its naming, ordering, privacy, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent embedded-runner history makes this person the strongest available owner for deciding the core lifecycle and diagnostics boundary.
